“Having built a stupa out of bricks for the Sage Atthadassi, the World’s Elder, the Neutral One;”
I had a walking path constructed;
five ratanas high,
that walking path was beautifully fashioned.
A hundred cubits in length,
delightful and worthy of cultivation—
this the Blessed One accepted.
Atthadassī, the supreme among men,
took some sand in his hand and spoke these verses.
“By this gift of sand and by this well-constructed walkway,
may I possess the seven treasures.”
He will enjoy the riverbank.
For three eons he will exercise divine sovereignty among the gods.
He will experience prosperity,
honored by celestial nymphs;
having returned to the world of men, he will enjoy success.
"He will become a king over the realm;
three times he will be a wheel-turning monarch throughout the earth."
Eighteen hundred aeons ago,
whatever deed I performed then,
I do not know a state of woe.
This is the fruit of the walking meditation path:
the four analytical knowledges, and so forth...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Caṅkamanadāyaka recited these verses.
This is the eighth legend of the elder Caṅkamanadāyaka.
